test_title: PYST 14: SSC CGL 2024 - General Knowledge (Held On: 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which Bill was passed by the Parliament, in July 2021, to help in the availability of working capital for the micro, small and medium enterprises sector?

options.text: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2021

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2021 was introduced to address the challenges faced by the micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in accessing working capital.
 
• Factoring is a financial transaction where a business sells its accounts receivable (invoices) to a third party (called a factor) at a discount in exchange for immediate money.
 
• This amendment widens the scope of entities that can undertake factoring business, thereby increasing the availability of funds to the MSME sector.
 
• The Bill aims to simplify the operational constraints in the factoring business and make it more accessible and affordable for MSMEs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Essential Commodities (Amendment) Bill, 2020**

 
 
• This bill aims to deregulate the production, supply, distribution, and trade of certain food items to increase the competitiveness of the market.
 
• It seeks to remove commodities like cereals, pulses, oilseeds, edible oils, onions, and potatoes from the list of essential commodities.
 
• This deregulation is expected to attract private sector/foreign direct investment into the agriculture sector.
 
 
 
• **The Minerals Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2020**
 
 
• This bill aims to promote ease of doing business in the coal and mining sector by amending the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, and the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015.
 
• It allows companies to participate in auctions of coal and lignite blocks even without prior experience in coal mining.
 
• The bill also removes the restriction on end-use of minerals produced from coal and lignite blocks.
 
 
 
• **The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2021**
 
 
• This bill introduces a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process (PIRP) for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
 
• PIRP is a quicker and cost-effective alternative to the normal Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC).
 
• This process allows MSMEs to restructure their liabilities and continue their business operations without undergoing a full insolvency process.
